A2 Key Paper 1 Reading and Writing Part 6 – Teacher’s Notes

Description

This is a guided discovery activity to find out what candidates need to do in A2 Key Paper 1 Reading
and Writing Part 6. Students look at two sample answers and discuss what makes a good answer at
this level. Finally there is an opportunity to write their own texts within a set time.

Time required:  25—35 minutes
Materials
required:        Student handout 1 and 2
                 Follow-up activity (optional)
Aims:            sample task

                 to familiarise students with A2 Key Paper 1 Reading and Writing Part 6
                
                 to raise awareness of the importance of identifying and addressing all
                 elements of a writing task.
                 to raise awareness of the factors which make a good answer at A2

                     Key level

Procedure

    1. Explain to students that they are going to do a short piece of writing. Point out that the
         message is similar to the texts that appear in the A2 Key Paper 1 Reading and Writing Part 6.
         These are based on emails, postcards or messages that A2 Key candidates are likely to write
         themselves. Give each student a copy of Student handout 1, write the following questions on
         the board and ask students to answer them:

          • Who are they writing to? (their English friend Toni)
          • What are they writing? (an email)
          • How many points do you need to write about? (3)
          • How many words should the write? (25 or more)

    2. Give your students Handout 2 with two sample answers. Point out that these were written by
         candidates and therefore are an indication of the level of grammatical accuracy required in the
         exam.

    3. Tell your students to decide which is the better answer. Write on the board the following
         questions which will help them decide:

 Have they written about all three points?
              Is it easy to understand what the writer means?
              Does the answer start and end in a good way?
              Are there any good words or phrases?
              Are any linking words used?
        4. Put your students into pairs and ask them to compare their answers. Using the key, go through
            the reasons why B is a better answer than A. Refer to the General Mark Scheme in the A2 Key
            Handbook for further information.
        5. Draw students’ attention to the length of the answers. In Part 6, candidates are advised to
            write between 25 and 35 words. They must write at least 25 words or they will lose marks.
            They will not lose marks if they write over 35 words but they should be encouraged not to
            write many more as this will increase the risk of making errors and including irrelevant
            information. It will also mean they probably spend too long on this part.

        6. Give out Handout 3 and tell your students that they are going to complete an example writing
            test. Set a time limit of 7 minutes, breaking it down into two minutes for the draft and then 5
            minutes to write the full email. Tell them that when writing the draft they do not write in full
            sentences but leave that for the email. The draft is to make sure that they cover all three
            points in their email. Tell your students when the two minutes are up so that they all have 5
            minutes to write the email.

Suggested follow-up activity

        1. Put each student with a partner. Students exchange their emails with their partner and write a
             reply email.

A2 Key Paper 1 Reading and Writing Part 6
Answer key
Key to procedure step 4
Sample Answer A – 3 marks
Sample Answer B – 5 marks

     Have they written about all three points?
           Sample answer A: no, the writer didn’t invite Toni to go swimming
           Sample answer B: yes, all points were covered

     Is it easy to understand what the writer means?
           Sample answer A: some effort is required of the reader, for example ‘swim to golden beach’
           Sample answer B: yes, the reader can easily understand the email

     Does the answer start and end in a good way?
           Sample answer A: it has an opening but no closing
           Sample answer B: yes, opening and closing ‘Hi Toni’, ‘Alex’

     Are there any good words or phrases?
           Sample answer A: yes, ‘I want to swim’
           Sample answer B: yes, ‘it’s faster and not expensive’, ‘nice weather’

     Are any linking words used?
           Sample answer A: no, sentences are short and simple
           Sample answer B: yes, simple linkers ‘so’ and ‘and’, most of the sentences are short but it has
           been written in a successful manner that communicates all three parts of the message.

Student handout 2
Compare the two answers below. One is a much better answer than the other. Which is better? Why?

A
From:
To:

Hi Toni
I am happy for your mail. I want to swim to golden beach on Saturday. We can go with a car from my father.
Are you OK?

29 words

B
From:
To:

Hi Toni!
Saturday will be a nice weather so I want to go swimming. Do you want to go with me? I want to visit a pool
in park. We can travel on the bus. It is faster and not expensive. What do you think?
Alex

46 words
